body: claimed: agy research (gemini) · 2026-11-27 05:32 UTC · plan: research

Research result: use ISO dialect M for the existing post. This recommendation preserves the maintainer's G83 decision in #2349.

I read our code and public Siemens manuals only. I read no HSMWorks or Fusion material. No control or simulator was exercised.

Code baseline: local HEAD `5fdbed9bd8e7a8bb28e6f162a02ab423842b77e8`.

### Answers to the open questions

1. Which command selects each mode?

`G290` selects Siemens mode. `G291` selects ISO dialect mode. Each selector needs its own block. `G291` does not select milling instead of turning. The machine configuration selects ISO dialect M or T.

Evidence: Siemens, *ISO dialects*, Function Manual, 07/2021, 6FC5397-7BP40-3BA2, sections 4.1 and 4.1.1, pages 19-21. The post emits neither selector in `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:317-330`.

2. Which mode accepts the words in the issue?

| Output | Siemens mode | ISO dialect M |
|---|---|---|
| `G73`, `G80`-`G89` drilling commands | Use native cycle calls instead | The ISO cycle family applies |
| `G700` / `G710` | Native length and feed units | Use `G20` / `G21` |
| `G505` / `G506` | Native settable frames 5 and 6 | Use the ISO work-offset selection scheme |
| `G41 NORM` / `G42 NORM` | Native approach behavior | ISO supports `G41` / `G42`; do not append `NORM` |
| `ROT RPL=...` / `ROT` | Native frame rotation | The ISO rotation commands are `G68` / `G69` |
| `MEAS=1` | Native measuring motion | Do not emit this native motion command in ISO blocks |
| `CYCLE832(...)` | A native cycle call | A Siemens subprogram call can be legal; see answer 3 |

Evidence: Siemens, *Fundamentals*, Programming Manual, 12/2018, A5E40869423B AB, sections 9.1, 11.2 and 13.5. These sections describe native offsets, approach behavior and rotation.

Evidence: Siemens, *ISO Milling*, Programming Manual, 07/2021, 6FC5398-7BP40-3BA2, sections 5.1.4, 5.1.9, 5.2.2 and 5.4; chapter 6; appendix B. ISO tool length uses `G43` with an offset selection. ISO drilling has `G98` and `G99` return modes.

Code: `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:356-398`, `:450-503`, `:685-795`, `:803-910`, and `:920-944`.

3. Does every Siemens-looking word prove a mode error?

No. The ISO Function Manual permits selected Siemens control structures and subprogram calls in ISO mode. See sections 4.1.1 and 4.4.2, pages 20-21 and 66.

Thus, `IF` and a `CYCLE832(...)` call need separate checks. Their spelling alone does not prove a defect. A permitted call does not prove that the installed cycle supports our arguments. The current smoothing arguments remain subject to that check.

The probing sequence also contains measuring motion, variable access, alarms and frame writes. Check the complete sequence before support is claimed.

4. Which design should this post use?

Keep the existing post in ISO dialect M. State `G291` before executable setup commands. Keep one explicit language in the generated main program.

Reason: #2349 records a machine check for `G83 P<ms>` in `G291`. The maintainer chose to keep that output. The record is now in `RECOMMENDED.md:54861-54919`; the original decision file was collected at the release cut. `docs/decisions/README.md` explains this process.

Do not convert the existing post to Siemens cycles in this first slice. That would replace the verified G83 interface. Do not add mode switches around individual features. They add frame and modal-state transitions to each feature combination.

The smallest useful slice supports ordinary milling and the current verified ISO drilling forms. It corrects the units, work-offset names, tool length and return mode. It refuses features that still require native output. It never removes a requested feature silently.

The machine must supply a valid ISO tool-offset mapping. Do not assume that an ISO H number equals a native cutting-edge number. The ISO Function Manual describes the mapping in section 5.1, pages 83-91.

Control compensation, control rotation, probing and smoothing need valid ISO output or a named refusal in this slice. A user can select baked rotation where the existing workflow permits it. Keep the G73, G84, G85 and G86 dwell refusals. Preserve the G83 exception from #2349.

5. What evidence must the implementation add?

Use complete programs, not a header-only assertion. Cover both units, offsets 1-6, tool changes, first motion, cycles, section changes and program end. Cover requests for each native feature. Confirm that each request has legal output or blocks program release.

Pin the selected cycle return mode and the existing seating behavior. Check program-end unit changes separately. Check tool-offset activation before motion. Do not rename G505 to G58 without checking the selected physical frame.

Existing test paths: `crates/post/tests/sinumerik_g83_dwell.rs`, `sinumerik_dwell.rs`, `script_sinumerik.rs`, `probe_dialects.rs`, `wcs_rotate.rs`, `work_offset_index.rs`, `comp.rs`, `end_units.rs`, and `setup_change.rs`.

The stream contract is in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md:44-65`. Cycle dispatch is in `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs:359-389`. A cycle record can exist without an expanded chain, so an empty cycle hook is not a safe fallback.

Coordinate with #4143 for tool offsets, #4144 for machine-coordinate retracts, and #4150 for G94. Do not duplicate their fixes.

### Concrete sub-issue

Title: Make the Sinumerik 840D post consistent with ISO dialect M

Action: Add an explicit ISO mode and make every emitted block valid for that mode, with named refusals for unsupported features.

Done means: Complete-program tests cover the mode, units, physical offsets, tool length, drilling, native-feature refusals and program end. G83 retains `P<ms>`.

Proposed labels: `P7`, `effort:high`, `area:post`, `source:agent`.

P7 marks the implementation follow-up in the requested P4-P8 range. The umbrella retains P3. Effort is high because the work changes posted G-code and refusal behavior.
